subject: Day 81: cause-and-effect play-gym
bodyText:
Today's focus
Avi is starting to link his own action to a result. A play gym where a kick or swipe produces a sound or light is the cleanest way to let him discover that he can make things happen, the foundation for intentional reaching.

Action items
- Set him under a play gym positioned so a kick or arm-swipe triggers a chime or light. When the same movement reliably produces the same result, he begins repeating the action on purpose rather than at random. AAP movement, birth to three months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-Birth-to-Three-Months.aspx
- Keep the pumping freezer stash building if you have returned to work. Aim for roughly 2 oz frozen per missed feed so a single off day does not put you behind.
- Confirm a childcare backup plan now: identify a backup agency or an on-call family member before you need one, since the first illness usually lands within two to four weeks of starting.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Frequent hand-to-mouth and looking intently at his own hands. This is normal sensorimotor exploration, not a problem to redirect.
- [monitor] Asymmetric movement, where he consistently favors one side or holds his head turned one way. Note it and raise it if it persists past a week or two.
- [call within 24h] A new feeding-refusal pattern or persistent crying that is unlike his usual fussiness.
- [call now] Fever of 100.4F rectal or higher under 90 days, or labored breathing. Page the pediatrician same-day and go to the ER if he is blue around the lips!

Enrichment opportunities
- Offer cause-and-effect play under the gym daily, and pause to let him work out the link between his swipe and the sound rather than triggering it for him. AAP movement, birth to three months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-Birth-to-Three-Months.aspx
- Let him track the hanging toys across his full visual field. He now follows the 180 degrees smoothly, so move a toy slowly from one side to the other and let his eyes lead. HealthyChildren baby senses: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx
- Pair the play-gym sounds with your own live singing, varying tempo from a slow lullaby to a faster clapping song. Live, participatory music drives prelinguistic communication far more than recorded audio. Gerry et al. 2012, infant music classes: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22490184/

Upcoming
- Day 84-91 (~3 months): sleep-consolidation window opens; start anchoring a loose, consistent sleep-wake routine.
- Day 112-126 (~4 months): 4-month well visit with RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2.
- Day 98-126 (~14-18 weeks): 4-month sleep regression typically begins.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at you, moves, or makes sounds to keep your attention
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Active engagement — baby is now driving the interaction, not just responding.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-to-get-attention/complete

- Pushes up on elbows during tummy time
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Tripod position. Builds toward eventual rolling.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/pushes-up-on-elbows/complete

- Holds a toy when you put it in his hand
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Voluntary grasp emerging. Soon followed by reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-toy-when-placed/complete

- Smiles on his own to get your attention
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Initiates the smile rather than responding to yours — emerging social agency.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/smiles-to-get-attention/complete

- Chuckles (not yet a full laugh)
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Throaty soft laugh sounds. Precedes the full belly laugh by a few weeks.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/chuckles/complete
